competitors.name: USGS/BLM Natural Gas Compositional Analyses Dataset (free)
competitors.what_they_do: Free, downloadable (CSV/Access) compilation of about 16,000 US well gas analyses, 1917-2021, with He, H2, N2, CO2 and hydrocarbons in mol %, plus lat/long, formation and API number where known. Built from the Bureau of Mines Federal Helium Program, the BLM, the USGS and state survey databases. A separate USGS helium-concentration dataset also exists. This is the single biggest substitute for the gas-analysis half of the pitch.

competitors.name: USGS Geologic Hydrogen Prospectivity Map Explorer
competitors.what_they_do: Free national prospectivity map for geologic hydrogen with 19 input layers and 7 integrated maps. It flags the Midcontinent and central California as high-prospectivity. It is regional, not well-level.

competitors.name: SMU / NGDS heat-flow and corrected bottom-hole-temperature database (now on the DOE Geothermal Data Repository)
competitors.what_they_do: Free download of heat-flow and gradient data for 44,000+ wells. It includes corrected bottom-hole temperatures for 30,000+ oil and gas wells. This already does the 'correct for known BHT bias' step for geothermal.
competitors.scale_or_funding: DOE-funded, free; moved to open access in 2026

competitors.name: Project InnerSpace GeoMap
competitors.what_they_do: Free, global geothermal resource and suitability map built with Google. It uses millions of thermal data points, including legacy well temperatures. In South America, Petrobras supplied structured well-temperature data that was otherwise scattered across thousands of well reports.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Nonprofit with Google partnership; global coverage completed

competitors.name: Zanskar
competitors.what_they_do: AI geothermal developer. It tracked down and digitized long-forgotten analog subsurface datasets and trained models on them. It keeps the data exclusive and uses it to find and build its own plants, so it is a vertically integrated developer rather than a data seller.

competitors.name: Koloma
competitors.what_they_do: Natural hydrogen exploration company. It uses proprietary and legacy exploration data with analytics to narrow down prospects, and has almost certainly mined old well records in-house.

competitors.name: HyTerra
competitors.what_they_do: ASX-listed junior with 80,000+ acres of Kansas/Nebraska leases. It began by twinning historic wells with hydrogen and helium shows, then moved to proprietary geophysics. It is the archetypal target customer and shows the play already exploits legacy shows without any atlas vendor.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Public junior; McCoy 1 well with up to 83-96% H2 (https://www.gasworld.com/story/hyterra-confirms-hydrogen-up-to-83-at-kansas-nemaha-project/2243371.article/)

competitors.name: MAX Power Mining (MAXX LEMI platform)
competitors.what_they_do: Junior explorer whose LEMI platform merges drilling, core, seismic and extensive legacy datasets to rank natural hydrogen and helium systems. This is another in-house version of the idea.

competitors.name: Terra AI
competitors.what_they_do: Generative subsurface modeling SaaS. It integrates geophysics, geochemistry and drilling data into probabilistic 3D models for mining, enhanced geothermal and carbon storage.
competitors.scale_or_funding: $20M Series A, June 2026, led by Khosla with BHP Ventures (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/terra-ai-raises-20m-to-accelerate-mineral-and-reservoir-exploration-to-meet-global-critical-mineral-and-energy-demands-302789531.html)

competitors.name: HyReveal (IORIGIN basin modeling)
competitors.what_they_do: Basin-modeling software for natural hydrogen and helium, founded by Viacheslav Zgonnik, author of the standard hydrogen-occurrence review. It can integrate existing datasets. It targets pure-play ventures and O&G operators.

competitors.name: Heologic Group
competitors.what_they_do: Helium-anomaly-based exploration and AI. It claims the largest digital subsoil helium-concentration database in the world and sells multi-resource exploration services covering helium, hydrogen and geothermal.

competitors.name: NthDS
competitors.what_they_do: AI digitization of legacy well files (mud logs, DST reports, core reports, wireline logs). It also runs a marketplace of 1.6M+ well LAS files at $70-80 per well. It has no hydrogen, helium or geothermal product today, but it owns the extraction capability and the O&G buyer relationships.

competitors.name: Enverus (with TGS North American well data business, acquired July 2026)
competitors.what_they_do: Incumbent oil and gas data vendor. Enverus Foundations covers hydrogen, helium, geothermal and DLE at project level, and its research team models natural hydrogen and helium economics. It bought the A2D well-log library and the TGS well data business, so it could add hydrogen and helium shows as a feature.

competitors.name: WellScout AI
competitors.what_they_do: Uses physics-informed neural networks on legacy well data to screen oilfield wells for geothermal conversion.

competitors.name: EPRI Naturally-Occurring Hydrogen site and Kansas Geological Survey OFR 2025-59
competitors.what_they_do: Free trackers of natural hydrogen companies and projects, plus the free Kansas gas-analysis research database (https://www.kgs.ku.edu/Publications/OFR/2025/OFR2025-59/index.html) compiled by David Newell. Both undercut a paid version of the easy layers.

competitors.name: AKAP Energy, Wood Mackenzie and Rystad (market intelligence)
competitors.what_they_do: Subscription market intelligence on natural hydrogen and helium projects, companies and economics. It is not well-level lead data, but it is the same buyer's analyst budget.

white_space: The wedge that remains is narrow but real. Nobody found sells page-level, provenance-linked hydrogen, helium and heat evidence extracted from the unstructured parts of old well files. That means mud-log gas shows, drill-stem-test and production-test reports, driller notes such as non-flammable gas, and water-well gas, all at lease-block or section level. The free datasets (USGS/BLM, SMU/GDR, KGS) already cover the structured gas-analysis and corrected-BHT layers, so a paid product cannot rest on those. The USGS roughly 16,000 He-bearing points and the 30,000 corrected BHT wells are a free baseline that any paid product has to beat. The Paris Basin OCR study found only 26 wells with H2 detection out of about 5,000 in the database (0.5%), which suggests few real leads per basin. Unserved specifics: (1) the 20-30 state and provincial archives whose scans are not yet digitized, with a defensible per-record confidence grade (sampling method, air contamination, analytical era); (2) one integrated He, H2 and heat layer, where the players found each cover a single commodity; (3) delivery to small juniors, landmen and lease advisors who cannot fund in-house teams. Koloma, Zanskar, HyTerra and MAX Power already do this in-house, so the addressable buyers are the smaller players (AKAP counts 123 companies in natural hydrogen, Rystad counted 40) plus the lease and land side.
evidence_of_demand: Partial and mostly indirect. I found no published price list or public purchase of a hydrogen/helium/heat atlas built from legacy wells. What exists: (1) Buyer count and money. Rystad counted 40 companies searching for natural hydrogen, up from 10 in 2020 (https://www.rystadenergy.com/news/white-gold-rush-pursuit-natural-hydrogen), and AKAP counts 123 (https://www.akapenergy.com/post/natural-hydrogen-exploration-surges-with-123-companies-engaged-in-the-sector). Zanskar raised $115M (https://heatmap.news/climate-tech/zanskar-series-c), Koloma about $245M (https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/hydrogen/the-245m-bid-to-pull-clean-hydrogen-straight-from-the-earth), Mantle8 EUR 31M (https://www.eu-startups.com/2026/05/frances-mantle8-raises-e31-million-to-fund-the-worlds-most-advanced-natural-hydrogen-exploration-and-drilling-campaign/), and Terra AI $20M (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/terra-ai-raises-20m-to-accelerate-mineral-and-reservoir-exploration-to-meet-global-critical-mineral-and-energy-demands-302789531.html). (2) Proof that legacy data drives discovery. HyTerra's Kansas program began with historic hydrogen and helium shows (https://fuelcellsworks.com/2025/07/09/clean-energy/hyterra-advances-drilling-campaign-at-kansas-nemaha-hydrogen-project-with-strategic-third-well). Zanskar bought and digitized analog datasets and struck the most productive pumped geothermal well in the US (https://heatmap.news/climate-tech/ai-geothermal-discovery). Petrobras handed structured well-temperature data to Project InnerSpace (https://www.thinkgeoenergy.com/project-innerspace-completes-global-geothermal-resource-map-with-geomap-europe/). (3) Proof that people pay for digitized old well data: NthDS sells LAS files at $70-80 per well (https://nthds.com/), and Enverus bought the A2D well-log library (https://www.enverus.com/newsroom/enverus-acquires-a2d-well-log-library-from-tgs-connecting-subsurface-data-to-energy-decision-workflows/) and then TGS's North American well data business (https://www.tgs.com/well-data-products/geological-data). (4) Government spend on digitization by state surveys: $2M NGGDPP in 2026, $5K-200K per award (https://www.highergov.com/grant-opportunity/2026-national-geological-amp-geophysical-data-preservation-program-361151/). This is more a substitute than a customer. Counter-evidence: the academic OCR and LLM methods are public (https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2024GC011501, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.05438). I found nothing showing juniors budgeting $15-50k per year for this kind of data.
sharper_angle: Do not sell a general atlas. Sell unstructured-evidence leads for one live fairway, with lease status attached. Start with the Midcontinent Rift and Nemaha corridor (KS/NE/OK, possibly MI and OH), where lease-taking is active now. Use VLM extraction to pull the things the free datasets omit: mud-log H2 and He shows, DST and production-test gas notes, driller remarks, and non-flammable or N2-rich gas indicators. Every lead links to the source page image, with a confidence score for sampling method, air contamination and analytical era. Overlay mineral ownership and lease availability at section level and sell to landmen, lease advisors and juniors as a list of sections to lease this month. Price per lead pack and lease-success fee rather than a per-basin subscription. Treat geothermal as a bolt-on, since SMU/GDR and GeoMap already give away corrected BHT and Zanskar is a competitor. Hedge by pitching the extraction pipeline to state surveys (NGGDPP funding) and to NthDS or Enverus as a data partner or acquirer. Validation test before building: ask 10 junior explorers or lease advisors to prepay for a $5k section-level pack. If fewer than 3 will, the demand is not there. As written (atlas from gas analyses and BHT), the idea should not be built, because the free USGS, SMU/GDR, KGS and GeoMap datasets cover those layers.
